title: Electrical cream separator coupled with vacuum filtration for the purification of eimerian oocysts and trichostrongylid eggs
protocol: Purchase two-week-old SPF Arbor Acres broiler chicks from Beijing Arbor Acres Poultry Breeding Co., Ltd.
House the chicks in isolators and feed them pathogen-free diet and water.
Inoculate broiler chicks with sporulated oocysts by oral gavage at 2.5 x 10^3 per chick.
Collect faeces at 5-9 days post-inoculation according to eimerian species requirements.
Use collected Eimeria mitis oocysts to spike other oocyst-free chicken faeces for seed-and-recovery experiment validation.
Reconstitute E. mitis oocysts from freshly experimental infections.
Mix each sample with known amounts of freshly collected oocysts.
Combine chicken or rabbit food with faecal materials in a 1:5 ratio.
For rabbit samples, mix faecal material with food in a 1:5 ratio.
Homogenize the seeded matrices with saturated NaCl solution at a 1\(80 g):12.5 \(920 ml) ratio.
Mix until the mixture is homogeneous using a suitable laboratory mixer.
Orally infect 3-month-old sheep with a single dose of 5,000 H. contortus third-stage larvae (L3).
Maintain infected sheep for 50 days post-infection.
Collect faeces from the sheep at 14-50 days post-inoculation according to experimental requirements.
Introduce faecal suspensions through the feed inlet of the cream separator machine under centrifugal force.
Allow the heavier liquid and faecal residue to pass to the distant regions of the bowl.
Move the lighter layer (oocyst- and egg-enriched layer) towards the center of the bowl.
Reprocess the heavier layer for maximal recovery rate, if necessary.
Blend the pellet with the fluid flotation medium for 1 min after reprocessing.
Collect any remaining parasite oocysts and eggs from the blended mixture.
Clean the conical bowl manually between runs or use a fully automatic centrifugal cream separator machine for continuous processing.
Put the rubber ring into the slot.
Mount the inclined discs sequentially.
Cover the discs with the separating plastic plate.
Cover the separating plastic plate with the bowl cover.
Screw the nut by hand.
Tighten the nut with a bowl wrench.
Install the assembled drum onto the spindle.
Install the heavier layer discharge part.
Install the lighter layer discharge part.
Install the cream separator container.
Close the cork of the cream separator container.
Turn on the cream separator and wait 30 seconds until it reaches maximum speed.
Pour the sieved faecal suspension into the cream separator container.
Open the cork of the cream separator container.
Collect the lighter layers.
Collect the heavier layers.
Boil the bowl components for 10 minutes after washing to switch between different species.
Adjust the lighter layer volume by turning the regulating screw clockwise for smaller volume.
Adjust the lighter layer volume by turning the regulating screw counterclockwise for larger volume.
Mix the oocyst-/egg-containing faecal material with saturated sodium chloride solution in the ratio of 80 g to 920 ml.
Blend the mixture for 1 minute to prevent trapping of oocysts and eggs.
Squeeze the blended mixture through four layers of cheese cloth.
Dilute and resqueeze any residue left on the cheese cloth.
Place the oocyst-/egg-containing faecal material in an electrical cream separator container.
Centrifuge the container at approximately 10000 rpm for 5 minutes.
Mix 80 g of faecal material with 980 ml of saturated salt solution (1:12.5).
Homogenize with a laboratory mixer until the mixture is homogeneous, approximately 1 minute.
Squeeze homogenate through four layers of wet cheese cloth immersed in saturated salt solution to remove large debris.
Repeat step using the residue on the cheese cloth and resqueeze again.
Mix the filtrate from previous steps.
Apply filtrate to the faecal suspension container of cream separator machine when it reaches maximum speed.
Collect lighter and heavier layers and pellet in separate containers.
Reapply the heavier layer as described above and the pellet (faecal residue) as above to increase recovery of oocysts and eggs from the faeces.
Apply cream separator machine-purified oocysts and eggs (lighter layers) to vacuum filtration for salt and fine debris removal using a suitable mesh sieve filter and plain tap water for 2 minutes.
Collect the accumulated oocysts and eggs using a plastic pasteur pipette.
Incubate eimerian oocysts in 2.5% potassium dichromate solution.
Incubate trichostrongylid eggs in distilled water.
Bleach collected oocysts with ice-cold household bleach (sodium hypochlorite, ~5% w/v aqueous) for 10 minutes on ice, shaking occasionally.
Wash bleached oocysts thoroughly under aseptic conditions.
Sterilize accumulated eggs by washing twice in 2% sodium hypochlorite for 20 seconds each.
Wash sterilized eggs five times with sterile distilled water under disinfected conditions.
Prepare buffered sucrose solution (PBS-Ca buffer, pH 7.4 plus 1 mM CaCl2).
Layer two consecutive solutions of different density (60% and 30%) in a 50 ml centrifuge tube.
Add phenol red to the 30% sucrose solution for easy discrimination between gradient layers.
Centrifuge the prepared gradients at 2000 rpm for 10 minutes.
Wash separated oocysts and eggs repeatedly with distilled water or suitable buffer under vacuum filtration.
Layer progressively less dense 30% sucrose solution upon 60% sucrose solution using a yellow pipettor tip attached to a blue pipettor tip.
Allow solutions to run down inside the pipettor tips steadily due to gravity.
Prepare a narrow band of oocyst- or egg- suspension (7.5 ml) on top of the gradient.
Centrifuge the gradient at low speed to allow oocysts and eggs to band at the interface between two densities.
Concentrate and recover eimerian oocysts and trichostronglyid eggs using sucrose step-density gradient centrifugation.
Filter the concentrated oocysts and eggs through a vacuum filtration system with suitable mesh sizes for fine debris removal.
Wash the filtered oocysts and eggs thoroughly with plain tap water.
Collect eimerian oocysts in 2.5% potassium dichromate solution.
Collect haemonchine eggs in distilled water.
Adjust the number of collected oocysts and eggs by centrifugation at 3000 rpm for 5 minutes.
Add the required volume of previous solutions to adjust the concentration.
Transfer freshly purified oocysts into a 2.5% potassium dichromate solution.
Cover Erlenmeyer flasks with perforated lids and place them on a rotary shaker at 26 °C and 80% relative humidity for approximately 72 hours.
Examine a drop from each aliquot under the microscope to confirm sporulation.
Consider oocysts as sporulated when four distinguishable sporocysts are visible in each oocyst.
Check at least five hundred oocysts in each aliquot for statistical analysis.
Record the number of sporulated oocysts and calculate the average viability rate using the provided formula.
Wash extracted nematode eggs on a 35 µm nylon filter with distilled water to remove fine debris and salt or sugar.
Adjust the egg concentration to 500 eggs per well in a 6-well cell culture plate containing distilled water.
Incubate the plate for 7 days at room temperature to allow parasite development to the L3 larval stage.
Record the total number of L3 larvae developed from the eggs.
Calculate the average viability rate using the provided formula.
